शौन शौन, अम्, n. (fr. शूना), meat kept
at a slaughter-house.

शौनिक, अस्, m. a butcher, poulterer, vender of
the flesh of beasts or birds; chase, hunting.

सौनिक, अस्, m. a butcher, vender of the flesh of
beasts or birds.

शौनक शौनक, अस्, m., N. of the reputed
author of the Ṛg-veda Prātiśākhya and of certain
Kalpa-sūtras and various other Vedic compositions
and works on law, (he is described as the teacher of
Kātyāyana and especially of Āśvalāyana; he is said
to have united the Bāṣkala and Śākala Śākhās,
and is sometimes identified with the Vedic Ṛṣi
Gṛtsa-mada; but according to the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa,
Śaunaka was a son of Gṛtsa-mada, and originated
the system of four castes; the various legends about
him are very confused.)
—शौनक-कल्प-सूत्र,
अम्, n., N. of certain Kalpa-sūtras (ascribed to
Śaunaka and supposed to have been destroyed by
the author).
—शौनक-गृह्य-सूत्र, अम्, n. the
Gṛhya-sūtras of the Ṛg-veda ascribed to Śaunaka.
—शौनकानुक्रमणी (˚क-अन्˚), f. an Anukra-
maṇī or Vedic index ascribed to Śaunaka.
—शौन-
कारण्यक (˚क-आर्˚), अम्, n. an Āraṇyaka ascribed
to Śaunaka (probably identified with the Aitareyā-
raṇyaka).
—शौनकोपनिषद् (˚क-उप्˚), त्, f., N. of
an Upaniṣad.

शौनकिन्, इनस्, m. pl. the pupils or followers of
Śaunaka.
शौनकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.

शौनकीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to or composed
by Śaunaka or the Śaunakīyas, (शौनकीय-च-
तुराध्यायिका, ‘Śaunaka's treatise in four chapters,’
i. e. the Atharva-veda Prātiśākhya); (आस्), m. pl.
the pupils or school of Śaunaka.
—शौनकीय-च-
तुराध्यायिका, f., N. of the above Prātiśākhya.
—शौनकीय-चरण, N. of a Caraṇa (probably
founded by the author of the Śākala-prātiśākhya).

शौनहोत्र शौनहोत्र, अस्, m. the son of
Śuna-hotra and grandson of Bharad-vāja; epithet of
the Vedic Ṛṣi Gṛtsa-mada.

सौनधर्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the law or rule of
butchery,’ a state of deadly hostility.

सौनन्द सौनन्द, अम्, n. the club of Bala-
rāma.

सौनन्दिन्, ई, m. ‘having Saunanda,’ epithet of
Bala-rāma, (see p. 675.)

सौन्दर्य सौन्दर्य, अम्, n. (fr. सुन्दर),
beauty, loveliness, handsomeness, gracefulness, ele-
gance.
—सौन्दर्य-लहरी, f., N. of a mystical
poem ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya (= आनन्द-लहरी).
शौनःशेप, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to Śunaḥ-śepa.
